solves: Shows a short sequence of slides of the same kind, one part at a time, for the person to go through at their own pace with arrows, indicators or by dragging.
use_when: For a short sequence of similar content where seeing one slide at a time is enough, such as an image gallery, featured cards or welcome steps.
Peek when you want to make clear there are more slides: the edge of the neighbor invites the person to move on. It is the recommended layout.
One slide when one at a time is enough; several when seeing some slides at once helps to choose.
With three to five slides, keep the indicators; with more than five, the indicators go off and the counter comes on.
Keep slides of the same kind and the same height, so the strip does not jump when the slide changes.
Put the text below the image, not over it: the contrast over a photo is not guaranteed.
Store the slide from the nph-slide-change event and give it back through index when the position has to be kept.
do_not_use_when: For a list or grid where the person needs to see or compare everything: show the items together.
To split a long list into pages: use nph-pagination.
To switch between named sections of a page: use nph-tabs.
To show the progress of a task: use nph-progress.
For two slides: show both together, side by side or in a list; only without room use arrows and indicators with two items.
For important content: a slide out of view is rarely seen.
For automatic rotation, a vertical carousel, thumbnails or wrap-around: they do not exist in v1.
Turning arrows and indicators off together, or leaving the sequence with no indicators and no counter.

layout.constraint: The Figma property `layout`. single is one whole slide at a time, as wide as the carousel; several shows as many whole slides as fit the carousel width, at least one, and a slide keeps the width of its content and is never cut; peek shows the whole current slide and the edge of the neighbor, carousel/peek-size wide. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the slide width by it. A value outside the list, or padded with whitespace, draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

index.constraint: The first slide in view, counted from zero. In single and peek it is the current slide. In several the current page is derived from it, and a resize never rewrites it nor fires the event. A number out of range shows the nearest slide, and the property keeps what was written. Setting it from code never fires nph-slide-change.

hide-arrows.constraint: The Figma boolean `setas` is on by default, so the property turns both arrows off. The property is hideArrows. With the arrows off and the indicators off there is only dragging left, and the carousel warns in development.

hide-indicators.constraint: The Figma boolean `indicadores` is on by default, so the property turns the indicators off. The property is hideIndicators. Turn counter on when the indicators are off.

counter.constraint: The Figma boolean `contador`. Shows "position of total" after the next arrow. With more than five pages it comes on by itself, in the several layout counting pages.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the region, already localized, such as Photo gallery. Without it, the host aria-label is used; without both the carousel warns in development.

previous-label.constraint: The name and the tooltip of the previous arrow. Without it, the default of the lang nearest to the carousel (Portuguese, English or Spanish), such as Previous slide. The property is previousLabel.

next-label.constraint: The name and the tooltip of the next arrow, such as Next slide. The property is nextLabel.

indicators-label.constraint: The name of the group of indicators, such as Choose a slide. The property is indicatorsLabel.

slide-label.constraint: The name of an indicator, a template with the placeholders position and total in curly braces, such as Slide 2 of 5. The property is slideLabel.

page-label.constraint: The name of an indicator in the several layout, where each one stands for a page, a template with the placeholder position, such as Go to page 2. The property is pageLabel.

position-label.constraint: The text of the counter and the name of each slide, a template with the placeholders position and total, such as 2 of 5. The property is positionLabel.

slot.constraint: The slides: the direct element children of the carousel, two or more, with free content. The carousel puts each one in its own box by manual slot assignment and writes no attribute on it. A slide has no background, outline or radius of its own: the content brings them. A text or a comment between the slides is not a slide. The carousel takes the width of its container; a slide keeps its own height.

nph-slide-change.constraint: Fired when the person changes the slide, by arrow, indicator, key or drag, once per change. It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and is not cancelable. detail.index is the first slide in view. Setting index from code, and a resize, never fire it.

layout.choose_when: peek to show there are more slides, the recommended layout; single when one at a time is enough; several when seeing some slides at once helps to choose.

controls.choose_when: Arrows and indicators for three to five slides. Counter instead of the indicators above five pages. Arrows alone, or indicators alone, only when one of them is enough.
do_not_combine_with: arrows and indicators both off: only dragging is left.

indicator.changes_for_user: A dot in a 24 by 24 target. The targets touch.

indicator-current.changes_for_user: A wider pill in the brand color. It is the cue besides the color, and it has no hover.

indicator-hover.changes_for_user: The target of the other indicators gets a background. Hover does not move focus nor change the slide.

indicator-focus.changes_for_user: By keyboard, a border outside the target and a halo beyond it, with no hover background.

arrow.token: the tokens of nph-button secondary solid circular, and carousel/control-foreground for the icon
arrow.changes_for_user: The icon-only button with a chevron. Hover turns the chevron solid.

arrow-disabled.changes_for_user: At the start the previous arrow and at the end the next one lose opacity and leave the Tab order.

counter.changes_for_user: The text position of total, after the next arrow.

business_rules: There is no wrap-around: the arrow on the side with no slide is disabled.
In single and peek a position is a slide. In several it is a page, of as many whole slides as fit the carousel width; the last page is aligned to the end, so it always shows whole slides.

In peek the current slide shows whole and the edge of the next one after it, in the middle and at the start; at the end, the edge of the previous one before it. The neighbor at the edge is out of view and inert.
A slide out of view is inert: its content leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree. In several every whole slide in view counts as in view.
Above five pages the indicators go off and the counter comes on by itself; with a single page there is nothing to go through, so no controls bar is drawn.
A resize changes the pages but never rewrites index and never fires the event.

A drag or swipe moves one step per gesture: past a quarter of a step, or a flick faster than 0.4 px per millisecond over at least 10 px. A drag shorter than 6 px is a click. The click that follows a drag does not reach the content. A drag that starts in a text field is left to the field.
The slide change uses motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing and is instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
Right-to-left text mirrors the slide order, the arrows, the keys and the drag.

tokens.arrow: carousel/control-foreground; the rest is nph-button secondary solid circular

ai_hints: Use nph-carousel for a short sequence of similar content seen one part at a time; for a list the person must compare, show the items together.
Put the slides as direct children of the carousel and give it a label, already localized.
Prefer layout peek for featured content, layout single when one at a time is enough, layout several when seeing some slides at once helps to choose.
Keep the slides the same height and put text below the image, never over it.
Keep at least one of the arrows and the indicators on; with more than five slides the counter replaces the indicators by itself.
Give the names already localized, or rely on the lang of the page; the templates take position and total.
Read the slide from detail.index of nph-slide-change, store it and give it back through index; the component keeps nothing.
Do not ask for automatic rotation, a vertical carousel, thumbnails or wrap-around: they do not exist in v1.

accessibility.semantics: A region with aria-roledescription carousel and a name. The track is aria-live polite. The indicators are a tablist of native buttons with role tab, aria-selected and aria-controls; each slide is a tabpanel with aria-roledescription slide named position of total (a group when there are no indicators). A slide out of view is inert.
accessibility.accessible_name: The region takes label or the host aria-label. The arrows take previous-label and next-label, which become the aria-label of the button and the tooltip text, with the icon hidden. Each indicator is named Slide N of total; in the several layout each one is named Go to page N. The tablist is named by indicators-label.
keyboard: Tab: the previous arrow, the indicators as one stop on the current one, and the next arrow, in this order; the links and buttons of the slide in view follow the content order.
Enter or Space on an arrow goes to the previous or the next position.
Left and Right on an indicator move the focus and show the slide; Home and End go to the first and the last. In right-to-left text the arrows mirror.
Click or tap on an indicator shows its slide.
Drag or swipe on the track changes the slide, never the only way.

Focus stays on the control used. A disabled arrow leaves the Tab order; when the focused arrow becomes disabled at an end, the focus moves to the current indicator, or to the other arrow when the indicators are off.
accessibility.focus: The arrow shows the focus of nph-button. The indicator shows a focus/border border outside its target and a focus/halo halo beyond it, with no hover background. The border passes 3:1 over color/background, color/card and color/muted in every brand and both schemes.
accessibility.contrast: The indicator, the current indicator and the arrow icon pass 3:1 over the surfaces named in the accepted frame; the counter passes 4.5:1. The current indicator over the hover background fails, so the current one has no hover. The disabled arrow is exempt.
accessibility.color_alternative: The current indicator is wider than the others, besides the color. The arrow on the side with no slide is disabled. The counter says the position in text.

invalid_combinations: A layout that is not single, several or peek — the carousel draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
Fewer than two slides — it still renders and warns in development.
A carousel with no label and no aria-label — it still renders and warns in development.
Arrows off and indicators off together, or indicators off with no counter — it still renders and warns in development.
Automatic rotation, a vertical carousel, thumbnails or wrap-around — they do not exist in v1.

children: nph-image for media and nph-skeleton while the content loads

anti_patterns: Turning arrows and indicators off together: only dragging is left, which not everyone can do.
Leaving the sequence with no indicators and no counter: the person does not know where they are.
Putting text over the photo: the contrast over a photo is not guaranteed.
Hiding important content in a carousel: a slide out of view is rarely seen.
Slides of different heights: the strip jumps when the slide changes.
Using the carousel for two slides, a list or a grid.
Using it for progress or named sections, where nph-progress and nph-tabs are the choice.
